runs.text: THE CORE IDEA

transcript.sourceText: THE CORE IDEA
transcript.text: THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: Long-run growth policy raises productive capacity rather than current spending alone. Saving and reliable finance support capital formation; education builds human capital; research and competition can advance technology. Stable property rights and institutions make firms more willing to invest. Because physical capital faces diminishing returns, sustained growth usually depends on several of these channels working together.

runs.text: Capital deepening from 20 to 40 units per worker raises output per worker from 28.53 to 36.37, a gain of 7.84. Because the curve flattens, capital accumulation alone faces diminishing returns. Sustained growth also requires human capital, technology, and institutions that raise productivity.
